about.title: Morgan Hill Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Morgan Hill's roads carry a steady mix of local traffic and drivers passing through on US-101, and that combination shows up in the numbers: 117 injury collisions and 160 people hurt in the most recent final reporting year, with three lives lost. Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. see a noticeable spike in reported crashes, often along corridors like Monterey Road, Butterfield Boulevard, and Dunne Avenue where commuter and local traffic overlap. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, the period right after matters. Insurance adjusters move quickly, and evidence like skid marks, vehicle damage, and witness memories fade fast. Our team handles car accident claims in Morgan Hill, evaluating the crash, dealing with insurers, and helping protect your right to recover for medical bills, lost income, and other losses. This is a free consultation — there's never an upfront cost to talk to us.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Dealing With the Insurance Company

items.title: California's Statute of Limitations Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim in California, but that window shrinks dramatically — sometimes to six months — if a government entity is involved, such as a poorly maintained city road. Waiting too long can cost you the right to recover anything at all.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce Your Recovery
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced by whatever percentage you're found responsible for the crash. An attorney can help make sure fault is assigned fairly and that early statements to insurers don't get used against you.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages, No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: California places no cap on compensation for pain, suffering, and other non-economic losses in most car accident cases. We work on contingency, so you don't pay anything upfront and owe nothing unless there's a recovery.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions in ways that can be used to minimize your claim later. We can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my accident happened at a Morgan Hill intersection with no clear fault?
items.answer: California's comparative fault rule means you can still recover compensation even if you share some responsibility for the crash, though your award may be reduced accordingly. This is common at busy corridors like Monterey Road or Dunne Avenue, where multiple factors can contribute to a collision. We can help gather evidence to establish what actually happened.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Nothing. Your initial case review is free, and there's no cost to have your case reviewed. We work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation.
